note: First successful llama.cpp run on Nemotron Nano 9B v2 -- llama.cpp correctly identifies the architecture as 'nemotron_h 9B Q4_K - Medium' (8.89B params, 6.28 GiB), confirming this build supports the hybrid Mamba-2/attention architecture natively. Run required copying the GGUF off the host's rotational E: drive onto WSL's native (SSD-backed vhdx) filesystem first -- the direct /mnt/e/ mmap path never completed even after ~13 CPU-minutes and was abandoned as the same 'intractable to benchmark' pattern this file's entry 1 already documented for 14B-on-WSL2-disk, just triggered here by a slow physical disk rather than by model size. See the paired tg32 run for the generation-side number and the actual headline finding (42.65 tok/s vs Ollama's ~12.7-12.9 tok/s on the same model).
